key_insight: Pre-AF 13 is an interpretable 13-feature model that uses routine discharge-report data to better predict atrial fibrillation risk in cardiovascular patients than common clinical risk scores.
clinical_relevance: This could help hospitals flag medium-term AF risk earlier in patients with cardiovascular disease, supporting targeted monitoring and follow-up.
method: Retrospective single-center EHR study of adults with cardiovascular disease and no prior AF.
NLP pipeline converted discharge reports into 73 structured features using rules plus transformer-based named entity recognition.
Built LightAutoML models: full, simple (Pre-AF 13), and linear bedside score (Pre-AF 9), with SHAP interpretation.
evidence_signal: Among 17,562 eligible patients, 1,438 (8.19%) developed AF; the simple model achieved ROC AUC 0.725 at 24 months and 0.696 over full follow-up, outperforming CHARGE-AF, C2HEST, MHS, and HAVOC.
watch_item: Because this was a single-center retrospective study, the model needs external validation before routine clinical use.
paper_title: Pre-AF 13: An Interpretable Atrial Fibrillation Risk Score Mined from Discharge Reports
